headline: Nothing about the game changed tonight. This was record keeping, plus one finding about our own tools that is worth knowing.
matters: Two things you asked for are now in place: the questions this lane needs you to answer are written out as real choices with costs, and finished work now publishes without asking you first. The finding is less comfortable. The way this editor describes how it finds the emulator looks like it was copied from another tool's documentation rather than measured against our own code, and that description has been handed to other lanes as fact for months. Nobody has checked it yet, and it is now written down as an open question instead of being quietly fixed.

headline: The editor was writing a background drift value the game could not read, and now it writes one it can. Every scene made in this editor carried it.
matters: When you set how far a background drifts up and down, the editor used to offer a list of named choices, and the name it started on was one the game reads as nonsense. The game did something that looked almost exactly like pinning the background still, with a one pixel wobble, which is why it went unnoticed. The setting is now a plain number box from 0 to 15, the saved test scenes that carried the bad value are corrected, and the scene built by hand in the editor was rebuilt in the editor rather than patched by hand. One thing is still unproven: nobody has watched the fix on real hardware or in the emulator, so what is certain is that we now write a value the game accepts, not yet that it looks right on screen.

headline: A moving background band built by hand in the editor now survives the whole trip into the engine's own tooling — and the test that was supposed to be checking this was broken.
matters: Until today the band path had only ever been proven with a band the code built for itself. Now one made the way an author would make it — typing the size, clicking Promote, pressing Ctrl+S — goes through the engine's own converter and comes out accepted, with the background picture pixel-for-pixel unchanged. The uncomfortable half: the check that judged this had a number typed into it that only matched one particular band size, so it called a perfectly correct result a failure, and would have done that for every band except the one it made itself. That is fixed and the fix is proven not to have made the check softer. Still not proven: none of this has been assembled into a ROM or run on the console, so the band has never actually moved on screen. Separately, the engine side has quietly fixed the thing that was blocking new bands: their art tool now keeps 128 tile slots back automatically. The existing background art has not been redone, so nothing is free yet, but the road you approved is now paved.

headline: The editor was telling agents the wrong size limits for a level's background — one too generous, one too tight.
matters: A background picture has a hard ceiling on how many unique tiles it can use, set by where the console keeps its sprite table. The editor told agents that ceiling was higher than it really is, so an agent could build a background the console physically cannot hold and only find out later, at bake time or as garbage sprayed over the sprites. In the same breath it was too strict about height: it insisted every background be half the height the engine actually supports, which made a full-height background impossible to author through the agent path at all — even though backgrounds that size already exist in the library. Both numbers now come from the shared file that records what the engine really does, so the limit the editor enforces, the limit it advertises and the limit the engine holds are one number that cannot drift apart. Before this there was not a single test anywhere covering reading or writing a background through the agent path; there are now, and I checked them by breaking the code on purpose and confirming the right ones failed. The one thing left unproven is a full-height background making the whole trip through a real save and into the engine's own tooling — that needs the app running, so I have written it down rather than implying the tests covered it.
detail: ROADMAP item 8, merged 06bb119 (fix 1d0a770, first tests 258ebab, docs 18f0574, two more stale comments 1d7f4f1, count correction 484254d). Height widening NOT blocked: every downstream stage already derives height; agent-handler was the only module believing 32 rows. Overseer verification on the merged tree: baseline on master 99bc74c measured firsthand at 4468 passed/3 skipped, merged 4488/3/0 (+20), tsc clean, build clean. Independently re-planted the tile ceiling (448->512): 3 rows red incl. one that discriminates 448 from the old 512, exact assertion 'promise resolved { tiles: 449 } instead of rejecting'; restored clean. Ran a DIFFERENT enumeration frame than the agent's (contract numbers as raw literals, any file type) to test their completeness claim: surfaced 0x7FF in bg-tiles.ts as a candidate duplicate, then dismissed it — 0x7FF is the VDP-wide 11-bit index field used at 17 sites incl. sprites and FG, not a BG-contract number, so leaving it unpinned is correct and pinning it would over-couple. bg-tiles.ts's BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT=1024 IS a genuine second copy and is pinned by drift test rather than imported, deliberately, since bg-tiles.ts is also the classic/S1 loader. Cross-repo sweep for get_bg consumers outside aurora: none read the reply's height field, so making it nullable breaks nothing (only hit is an empyrean status-audit doc listing the method name).

headline: I tried to build a ROM with a moving background band. It doesn't build — and finding out why was the point.
matters: Nobody had ever put an editor-made animated background into an actual ROM, so nobody knew what would happen. I did, and it stops in two places, both on the engine side. First, the engine's tool writes a reference to the animation artwork in a form the assembler won't accept — I found the correct form by looking at a neighbouring file doing the same job, and confirmed it fixes that step. Second, the table that decides how much room each piece of the ROM gets allots this feature exactly two bytes, because two bytes is what the switched-off version takes up; a real band needs about eight thousand. Neither problem is ours and neither could have been found any other way than by trying. Along the way I told you two things that were wrong: that there was spare room nearby (there isn't — what looked like spare room is other artwork, including the very background tiles this whole effort has been about), and that the knock-on effect was contained (it isn't, though it turned out smaller than feared — five pieces shift, not fifteen, because a sound-related address is pinned in hardware and absorbs the rest). The engine lane is doing both fixes as one job. When it lands I run this again and you finally get to watch the background move.

headline: A background parallax scene you build in Aurora now reaches the game running in the emulator.

Two engine-side gaps were found and fixed on the way (a missing layout-table row for the first real scene, and the engine preferring its built-in preset over the editor's choice) — both aeon's, both done tonight.

Until tonight a band had never actually run: the editor could save one and the tooling would accept it, but nothing had ever assembled it into a ROM or seen it move. Now the canopy in the jungle level animates, all eight of its frames play in order, and the picture underneath is untouched. You can look at it when you wake — and the same route now works for any band you author.

headline: You can now set how fast a background band moves. Until today every band the editor made ran at exactly one speed.
matters: This was the one gap left by the band you watched animating in the game last night — that band was supposed to move at a chosen speed and the panel had no way to say so, so it took the default. The control warns you that the number runs backwards: a higher setting is a SLOWER band, which is the opposite of what a speed field usually means. Leaving it alone keeps the key out of the file entirely, so a band you never thought about the speed of keeps following the engine's own default instead of being frozen to today's value.

headline: Bands now move inside the editor — and building it turned up that the editor has been showing a different background than the game builds.
matters: You asked to preview how the bands move without going to the emulator. That works now: switch on 'Play bands' and a timer band animates, while a camera-driven band correctly does NOT move on a clock — it moves when you pan, because that is what drives it in the game. With the preview off the viewport costs nothing, exactly as before. The catch is the finding underneath: the picture on the map canvas and the background the ROM is built from are two different files that nothing has ever connected, so on your real project the preview refuses rather than guessing. It says why on screen. Which of the two backgrounds should win is filed as d-11 and is yours to answer.

headline: The map now shows the background the game actually builds — and it turned out background painting had never reached the game at all.
matters: This is the call you made today. The editor had been drawing a stale copy of the jungle background while the game was built from a different one, with about 30% of the tiles disagreeing. It now draws the real one, so the band preview works on your actual level instead of refusing — I ran it and the band animates. The unplanned part: because painting wrote to whichever background was on screen, every background tile anyone has ever painted in Aurora went into a file the game does not read. That is now fixed in the same change. One thing is deliberately refused rather than quietly fixed: the tile picker still offers the whole zone tileset while this background only has 320 tiles, so picking one outside that range paints nothing and says so on screen, naming the file and the fix. Booked as its own item because it was equally wrong before today and is not this change's to hide.

headline: The map now shows you the background the game actually uses — and painting it finally changes the game.
matters: You had two copies of the Oracle Jungle background and they were not the same picture. The editor drew one; the ROM was built from the other. About 1,200 of the map's 4,096 background squares showed different artwork from what the console would show, and nobody could have spotted it by looking. That is now over: the map paints what ships. The moving-band preview you asked for, which refused to run on your real project for exactly this reason, now runs on it and the band moves. The uncomfortable half is what we found on the way in: painting the background in the editor has never reached the game. It edited a picture file the engine does not read, so every background stroke anyone has ever made was thrown away at build time. That is fixed in the same change — a stroke now edits the file the ROM is built from, and you can see it land. And one thing is now refused out loud instead of quietly going wrong: the tile chooser in background mode is showing you the FOREGROUND tiles, which are different art, so about two thirds of the tiles you could pick do not exist in the background at all. Picking one of those used to write a number the console would turn into garbage; it now paints nothing and tells you why. Giving background mode its own tile chooser is written down as the next job rather than bodged in here.

headline: The visual band tool you asked for cannot work the way it was specced, and we found that out in an afternoon instead of after building it.
matters: Boxing a region of the background and turning it into an animated band was going to be the other half of the map-preview work. It cannot resolve: the background's tiles are stored across-then-down, while an animated band needs them down-then-across, so a box you draw almost never names a range the engine can animate. At the size both your shipped bands use, it never does. The measurement is banked with the script that produced it, and the shape of the feature is out for a decision rather than being quietly changed into something buildable.

headline: A pinned copy of the engine stopped being able to rebuild its own ROM, and nothing in it looked wrong.
matters: We measure things by building a pinned copy and watching the result. That method quietly assumed the pin still builds to the pin, and it does not — so a future session could have compared against tonight's numbers, found a mismatch, and had nowhere to look. Now it is written down with a cheap defence.
detail: Clean tree throughout, every tracked file byte-perfect including the injector outputs the re-bake reproduced exactly. Drift is in gitignored artifacts every build regenerates (compression dictionary, sound blob) that the checkout shipped in a state the tools do not reproduce. 1273 bytes differ, first at the header checksum, scattered over 168KB — a re-pack signature, not a content change. Relayed to aeon with what I did NOT establish stated. docs/reviews/2026-08-27-fixture-build-drift.md.

headline: A finding I sent another lane last night was wrong about its own cause, and chasing that down found the real one: our test builds are not as repeatable as everyone assumed.
matters: When we pin a copy of the game's code to measure against, we do not pin the tool that builds it — so the same unchanged code can build into a different ROM hours later, with nothing on screen to say why. It has not corrupted any result we relied on, and there is now a free check that catches it.
detail: docs/reviews/2026-08-27-fixture-build-drift.md, corrected at aurora b1c15d0 (pushed). My packet's premise ('the checkout SHIPPED gitignored artifacts') was false and uncited; the aeon lane accepted it and built a correct-but-inapplicable cp -r explanation. Reflog shows the fixture is a git clone; git ls-tree dcc692d1 tracks no s4.bin and no engine/{debug,sound}/generated. Real varying input: build.sh takes SIGIL_EMIT (:317, writes engine/sound/generated) and SIGIL_BUILD (:558, the assembler) from the environment, both in sigil's live tree, neither pinned. Both rewritten inside the build window (emit_sound_blob 01:41:19, sigil 03:14:00) between crc 4b4f1b5b and f33b157e. Not closed: mtime proves a rewrite, not a behaviour change, and the old binary is gone. Defence adopted: record build.sh's own 'Assembler: sigil <rev>' banner beside every CRC. Relayed to aeon (whose queue it is) and sigil (whose binary it is).

headline: The example background scene is re-recorded at the editor's real 16-layer limit and now exercises the wobble controls — and a check that had been passing on luck was found and fixed.
matters: Two things. The recorded example scene had drifted: it was recorded when the editor allowed 8 layers and the limit is now 16, and it could not exercise any of the wobble controls that shipped this morning. Both are fixed, so the example now reflects what the editor actually offers. And reviewing it turned up something worse in the recording script — a workaround for a bug that had since been fixed had quietly become a bug itself, and every green run for months had been green by coincidence rather than because the thing it checked was true. That one was found by reading; no amount of running could have surfaced it.
detail: ROADMAP rows 60 DELIVERED and 61 booked; merged, plus overseer commits 2748dd4 (row 61) and 93691c6 (the harness fix). origin/master 71f8925 -> 93691c6, ls-remote confirmed. Agent delivered commits a451a9d (ceiling) / 6bab090 (deform gestures) / afdcbbb (packet), deliberately split so each has an interpretable delta: the one-line corroboration every previous re-origination used is unavailable at 43 lines, so each commit carries a delta PREDICTED IN WRITING BEFORE THE RUN (scratchpad/predict-commit{A,B}.py) and matched with no diff. I verified the predictors are non-circular (they read nothing from the app or the fixture) and that PREDICTED-commitB.json is byte-identical to the shipped fixture. Fixture 933 -> 2411 B, blob 893cd055 -> 4022f564, sha256 073283c6. VERIFIED FIRSTHAND ON THE MERGED TREE: vitest 5070 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed / 387 files, tsc exit 0, and an INDEPENDENT harness run by the overseer (own aeon copy, own port) 37/37 byte-identical to the committed fixture, aeon live scenes md5-unchanged. TWO FINDINGS THE AGENT DID NOT ABSORB: my brief's own prediction of v_factor was WRONG (R7's 'v_factor = layer count' is unsatisfiable at 16 — range 0..15, clamp lands on 15 which is the lock sentinel AND the new-scene default R7 forbids; proven by plant emitting v_factor:15, amended to the modulo R5/R6 already use), and a FIFTH rot (R4 had been driving nothing since tooltips landed, byte-invisible because addLayerCommand's default IS i*32, so row 5b was non-discriminating and always was). SIXTH ROT, mine, found in review: the CollapsibleSection workaround outlived its fix (5041f6e), its probe was end-anchored so open() could only return false, it therefore clicked every call and the section ended open only on even parity, and row 4b accepted 'clicked' as proof of openness. Red-first: restoring the old probe reddens 4b at 36/37 with every gesture row still green. AEON CROSS-LANE: aeon confirmed the v_factor sentinel is a genuine trap in THEIR contract (parallax.emp:1661, s1==15 returns 0 = LOCKED, so a clamping producer authors a band that does not move), booked in this lane's name, and accepted the argument that moving the sentinel beats a note-to-producers because a forgotten rule yields a silently wrong ROM while a moved sentinel fails loudly at build time.

headline: Checked that a scene the editor accepts is one the ROM build actually accepts — and found one place where it isn't.
matters: The editor blocks or warns about certain background scenes because the ROM build would reject them. Those warnings were written by reading the engine's source, and nobody had ever checked them against a real build. Good news first: every rule is still exactly where the editor thinks it is, so nothing has silently drifted. The gap is in the direction nobody had tested — one setting the build rejects outright, where the editor says nothing at all. It's an unusual case (the value has to arrive in a file rather than be picked in the app), but an author hitting it gets a broken build and no explanation. Booked with two smaller ones.
detail: Verification parcel, merged and pushed; origin/master 6dd5a55 -> d1617ae (ls-remote confirmed). Agent commit f702be4 (packet + rows 62/63), overseer commit for row 64 + a provenance correction. NO SOURCE CHANGED — verification parcel by design. All five guards verified in place against aeon HEAD; I re-read three of them firsthand in aeon's source rather than accepting the table. FRAMING CORRECTION that changes how the result reads: four of five guards are ADVISORY by row 58's deliberate design (a warned scene still saves), so 'Aurora refuses' means the check fired, not that the editor prevented anything; only sprite_mask is a prevention. DIRECTION 2 LICENSED BY A POSITIVE CONTROL (aeon's warning, relayed mid-parcel): hand-written JSON bypassing Aurora entirely, built rc=1 quoting guard 1's own interpolated signature — without it every clean cell would have been an empty-test pass. Row 62: sprite_mask is the one genuine permissive gap. Row 63: the period control accepts 1..256 where only the 9 divisors of 256 are legal; two parcels had independently worked around it. Row 64 (mine): guard 5 is FOUR ensures and Aurora covers three — scene_dsl.emp:1251 has no apparent counterpart, booked at READ-not-measured status because the packet had left it as an UNVERIFIED cell, which is invisible to a later session in a way a row is not. Corrected in the fixture provenance: the period rule's owner is the ENGINE (parallax_dsl.emp:52/:87) not sigil, and the divisor is a literal 256 not a derived table length; emitted values unaffected. factor0_lock divergence re-checked and still stricter-not-permissive ({15,15,0} builds green, crc=e9e07375, while Aurora warns). Discipline: banner revision fbf60abd on all 27 invocations, no cargo in sigil, aeon md5-identical before and after, green baseline first and restore-green after each of 13 refusals. Suite 5070 passed / 0 failed on the merged tree.

headline: The three gaps between what the editor allows and what the ROM build accepts are closed — including a second silent one that turned out to be real when measured.
matters: The editor now speaks up in every case where the build would reject your background scene. One of the three was booked as a suspicion rather than a fact, and measuring it confirmed it: a scene combining a curve with a moving anchor builds broken while the editor said nothing. Also, the box for the wobble's period used to offer 256 values when only 9 of them are legal — two separate pieces of work had quietly steered around that without anyone writing it down. Separately, this parcel caught the shared assembler being rebuilt underneath it by another part of the project; that turned out not to have damaged anything, but it changed how the three repos pin that tool.
detail: ROADMAP rows 62/63/64 DELIVERED, replaced in place; merged and pushed, origin/master f2cfeba -> c1addb9 (ls-remote confirmed). Agent commits a845770 (62) / d58fb6d (64) / 1b82251 (63) / e0b1ec5 (packet + harness). ROW 64 MEASURED, not assumed: curve on layer 3 + anchor dsa 3 / dsb 2 builds rc=1 quoting scene_dsl.emp:1251 verbatim while Aurora returned []; the 15/15 anchor (the case the guard PERMITS) builds green at crc=4362a054 and the no-curve control at 55e6ebbc, so the sentinel trap was real and a saturating fixture would have authored the permitted case while believing it authored the refused one. Why it had been dropped: guard 5's other three ensures are per-layer, this one has its halves on different objects (curve on a layer, shifts on the scene's anchor). ROW 63: select over computed divisors, carried non-divisor rendered DISABLED rather than silently displayed as legal; schema read first and it is the looser document (1..256), so this is deliberately stricter than the contract on the codebase's own test. ROW 62: advisory added, disabled option KEPT — they cover authoring versus arriving. 9 red-first node plants with distinct quoted failures, 4 in-app plants each taking only their own rows red, non-discriminating rows disclosed with catchers named. CROSS-LANE INCIDENT: the shared sigil binary was relinked twice mid-parcel (fbf60abd -> 52882e2e -> 537869e6, mtime 07:20:23) by another lane's cargo test --release --workspace; verified firsthand here and relayed to aeon and sigil unprompted. aeon confirmed no straddle (all seven goldens captured and restored six minutes before the first relink) and their attest incidentally ran a seven-shape equivalence check between the two revisions, 4023 passed. Both lanes adopted an md5-of-the-binary pin alongside the revision, on the argument that a revision names a property of the SOURCE and cannot detect a relink of the ARTIFACT; sigil also widened its announce rule from bilateral to all-lanes because this lane was mid-build and in none of that conversation.

headline: Proved you can actually reach the last two background controls in the app — and did it with a test instead of a second recorded scene that would have billed us forever.
matters: This repo has shipped a feature nobody could reach before: fully tested, working code with nothing in the app that called it. So 'can an author actually get to this control' is worth proving rather than assuming. Both remaining controls check out. The way it was proved matters as much: the item as booked called for recording a second example scene, which sounds cheap but obliges us to re-record it every single time the file format changes — that happened twice yesterday. A test carries the same claim once. The test is only worth anything because unwiring the control makes it fail while 'the control is on screen' keeps passing — which is the difference between proving reachability and proving a box exists.
detail: ROADMAP row 61 DELIVERED in the RULED shape, replaced in place and leading with the shape so nobody reads it as the booked version having been done; merged and pushed, origin/master 1330a77 -> pushed (ls-remote confirmed). Agent commits 523d08d (harness + select-key probe) / a2fc9ba (packet + row). git diff master -- src/ test/ is EMPTY. VERIFIED FIRSTHAND ON THE MERGED TREE: tsc exit 0, vitest 5074 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed, and I re-ran scratchpad/curve-vsplit-reachable-harness.mjs independently against my own aeon copy for 30/30 (dpr 1, load 4.78, uptime 2d 8min), aeon effects md5 unchanged. THE LOAD-BEARING PLANT: curve picker's onChange unwired -> 25/30 with 3c/5a/5d/6b/8a red, while 3a (control rendered and enabled, 18 options) and 7a (blanket no-missed-gesture) STAYED GREEN — if the rows were proving 'a control is on screen' that plant would have been all-green. Four more plants incl. the vsplit spinner pointed at world_y (27/30, 'layer top unchanged at 170') which rules out the measures-the-wrong-quantity cause, and two instrument plants reproducing the exact end-anchored-selector shape of the five real rots. Every asserted value is one the defaults cannot produce, including through the seed trap one field over: vsplitFromToggle seeds at = world_y (the i*32 trap), so the seed is read out of the document BETWEEN gestures and rows assert movement from it; the vsplit values are strictly interior to 0..511 so no clamp and no 15-family sentinel can land there. Non-discriminating disclosed: the 'and is ENABLED' clause of 3a/4a cannot fail today because the panel never passes disabled to either control; catchers named. Measured instrument limit reported rather than hidden: a <select> cannot be driven by arrow keys through CDP here (Chromium's menulist opens a native popup outside the page); typeahead works and is path 2's gesture, and the probe is committed so it is re-derivable. Nothing tagged for foreground follow-up.

headline: The build console no longer covers the properties panel — with it open, 94 of 126 controls could not be clicked.
matters: Every time a build failed the console appeared over the right-hand panel and hid the bottom of it, so controls you could see could not be clicked and scrolling would not reach them. That is exactly when you most need the panel. It now takes real space instead of floating over everything, so the column shrinks and everything stays reachable. Also landed earlier: the layer guides now sit on the background instead of sliding with your view, and adding a band selects and scrolls to it.
detail: ROADMAP row 68 DELIVERED; merged and pushed, origin/master dee1274 -> pushed (ls-remote confirmed). REPRODUCED ON MASTER FIRST, which the previous attempt at this skipped: 13/17 rows with 5a/5b/5c/8a red, 94 of 126 enabled column controls unreachable with the console open vs 0 shut, column box height 742 in BOTH states because the console was position:absolute left:0 right:0 height:260 zIndex:40 reserving no space. CAUSE FIX: BuildPanel becomes a flow child of the app root (flexShrink:0, maxHeight:50vh); column 742 -> 482 -> 742, canvas bottom 848 -> 588. The magic bottom:22 removed — measured wrong by 2px and underivable. Rejected: bounding the overlay to the column's edge (no width constant; Panel width is per-facet, and it would still cover canvas and Explorer) and padding the scrollers (workaround, two of them). VERIFIED FIRSTHAND ON THE MERGED TREE: tsc clean, vitest 5108 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed, and I re-ran the harness independently for 21/21 — at dpr 1.35 where all the agent's nine runs were dpr 1, so the fix is now covered on both device scales this environment produces. Plants: A (defect restored on both the 17-row and 21-row instruments) reds the four catchers verbatim plus the Home-tab row; B (delete maxHeight) reds 9a/9b, without which those rows assert only 260<=260. Five alternative green-paths ruled out on 5a. Console's OWN usability asserted separately (close button, pulled-to-top error line, 140th output line). One row DELETED rather than weakened: 'the lowest control sits above the console top' is false of a healthy app. Trade disclosed: console now flush with the window bottom, status bar above it. Booked not fixed: minHeight:0 still missing from App.tsx's flex chain — a real latent hazard, deliberately not bundled because no row here can see it and bundling it is what produced my reverted branch.

headline: The canvas now shows what the game would show — the frame is the camera, and each band slides at its own real speed.
matters: You can drag the screen frame and watch the background bands separate the way they will in the ROM, without leaving the surface you edit on. Two things you reported are fixed with it: the guide lines no longer get dragged around when you move the frame (they belong to the artwork, not to the screen), and the frame's vertical position is now a real scene value you can move — which is what was stopping you placing a layer down in the flowers. Arrow keys nudge the camera a pixel at a time, because a slow band only moves one pixel per sixteen and a mouse drag jumps straight past it.
detail: ROADMAP rows 69-71; merged and pushed, origin/master 8105673 -> pushed (ls-remote confirmed). Agent branch feat/camera-preview, six commits. VERIFIED FIRSTHAND ON THE MERGED TREE: tsc clean, vitest 5174 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed (65 new rows), and I re-ran scratchpad/camera-preview-harness.mjs independently for 26/26 at dpr 1.35 under load 13.2. FOUNDATION CORRECTION I sent mid-parcel, three of four points confirmed by the agent against source: .v_locked does move.w pcfg_v_offset -> Vscroll_BG and Camera_Y is never read on that arm, so a locked scene's layer tops are PLANE ROWS with guide origin 0 — guides no longer ride the frame. MY POINT 3 WAS WRONG and the agent said so rather than implementing it: the clamp was never a fixed 3..223, row 66 already shipped max(0,3+vo)..min(511,223+vo); the actual blocker was the guides plus v_offset having no gesture on the canvas at all. Decoder transcribed from Decode_Factor_A term for term, 16/16 agreement with the published FACTOR_* names, with the honest non-agreement disclosed: asr.w truncates PER TERM, so camX 7 through FACTOR_3_4 gives 6 rather than 5.25 or its floor 5. The 15-sentinel is numerically invisible for camX 0..32767 (x>>15 == 0), so it is caught structurally and via the vertical sentinel instead — stated rather than papered over. Arrow keys 1px, 16 with Shift, derived: 16 is the camera move that displaces FACTOR_1_16 by exactly one pixel. A row the agent had labelled a catcher came back GREEN under a plant (it moved the camera horizontally while the rule reads the frame's Y — failure mode iii verbatim); relabelled non-discriminating with 5e named as the catcher. NOT REPRODUCED and printed on the canvas per scene: curve ramps, deform, transitions, Plane A factors, sprites, priority, the left partial column. Two carry-forwards: Input.dispatchKeyEvent never replies on this CDP target and without a per-call timeout yields a process that exits 0 having reported nothing; and the aeon-tree md5 this role reports was walking other agents' nested worktrees because -path ./.git -prune only prunes the top level.

headline: The editor can now show you which foreground art draws in front of Sonic.
matters: The lens already existed and worked — it had simply never been switched on for the engine you use, so the answer was one line away and nobody could see it.
detail: aurora master 121521e2; showPriority added to OVERLAY_KEYS_BY_ENGINE.aeon; depiction lifted into tile-lens.ts shared with classic; CDP harness 24/24 re-run by the overseer on the merged tree; veil density measured at 24% of painted art at 100% zoom.

headline: Collision angle marks were drawn MIRRORED on the aeon map, and now lie along the slope with a barb showing the solid side.
matters: Every sloped angle mark pointed across the surface it described instead of along it, so the view was actively misleading while looking authoritative. 'Collision angles view is just bad' was a correct bug report, not a matter of taste.
detail: aurora master 121521e2; one mark module drawn by all five surfaces (both map overlays, picker thumbnails, big preview, paint ghost, legend); tangent from the angle byte, open side from the height sign; 6 unit guards red-first, CDP harness 18/18 re-run on the merged tree.

headline: Pasting now shows the art you copied, selections can be made per tile, and undo actually redraws the map.
matters: Undo after a paste was reverting the data but never repainting, so the screen kept showing art that was no longer there — you would have been editing against a map that disagreed with the file. It affected chunk stamps too, not just paste.
detail: aurora master 121521e2; batch commands were skipped by the renderer-cache listener while the sibling store-version path recursed; manual per-callsite workarounds deleted; tile-granular selections carry art only, keyed on rectangle alignment because collision is stored per 16px cell; CDP harness 34/34 re-run on the merged tree.

headline: A parallax layer guide now says why it stops moving, and dragging one is no longer trapped by the window.
matters: Two separate things were happening at once: an invisible legality limit that moved when you moved the view box, and a drag that really was imprisoned by the canvas edge. Your reading of it was half right and I had called it wrong.
detail: aurora master 1f65b3a; floor measured as EFFECTS_FIRE_LINE_MIN + v_offset at two offsets (67 at 64, 138 at 135) matching the field report; window mousemove added for guide drags only (a control layer left at vp.y+10=210 instead of 150); the v_offset path can still strand a placed layer below its floor and now surfaces it rather than silently re-clamping; CDP harness 46/46 re-run by the overseer on the merged tree, suite 5277 passing.

headline: The test suite is fully green, and the one failure everybody had been calling harmless was ours.
matters: A test was comparing our file-writing against a document sitting half-edited in aeon's folder, so it changed colour as someone else typed. Before today it had been green for its whole life while proving nothing, because it had no fixed thing to compare against. Four readers in a row waved it through.
detail: aurora master 84c23bf3; fixture vendored at aeon 88909bb3 with a provenance sidecar and a separate currency check that compares content not commit ids; verified by the overseer with no aeon present at all (passes, currency skips loudly) while aeon's file was still dirty, and by planting a one-token drift (fires, naming revision and blob). Suite 5281 passed / 0 failed. A second identical live-tree read was found that nobody had noticed, and two long-silent skipped blocks made audible. 37 reads of the s1disasm tree reported and deliberately left open rather than half-fixed.

headline: Painting a tile no longer wipes its priority or its flips, and you can now set them on purpose.
matters: Every tile you painted was silently losing its depth and its mirroring — so art you had set to draw in front of Sonic quietly dropped behind him, with nothing on screen to show it had happened. Four places in the app did it, not the two I found.
detail: aurora master 7c9090a; new brush-word rule module — flips come from the brush (a flip is which picture you picked), priority is tri-state defaulting to keep, chosen because a wrongly-kept priority shows up under the new lens immediately while a wrongly-cleared one is invisible until a player walks behind something. Controls copied from the classic facet's existing chips rather than invented. Harness 21/37 on the broken build, 37/37 fixed, re-run by the overseer on the merged tree; suite 5300 passing, zero failures. Open: the agent-facing paint-region call still flattens omitted attributes.

headline: A band's curve is now something you can see — and the camera preview had been painting itself black under a common setting.
matters: You could set a curve and the preview kept drawing the band flat, so the value was authorable and invisible. Worse, the whole in-frame composite was being drawn and then covered over on every frame whenever the Bg Plane overlay was off — it reported itself as working, with thousands of tests green, and showed nothing.
detail: aurora master 02f0117e; the deferral reason on record ('needs a clock') was wrong — read the engine source, the ramp depends on position not time, while deform genuinely does need a clock and had been lumped with it. Ramp is transcribed from the engine rather than interpolated, because it ramps a negated scroll word and floor division is not symmetric under negation. Roadmap's 'sine params or 256-point freehand' corrected — that text described a different feature's tables. Harness 29/29 re-run on the merged tree, suite 5310 passing, zero failures.

headline: You can now see where a vertical split actually lands down the frame, instead of typing a number into a spinner.
matters: A split's number was never a position — it is the background row you scroll TO, not the line it fires at. The two were easy to confuse and nothing on screen distinguished them; the strip now shows both, and refuses to place a split at all on a scene whose background scrolls, because there the line does not exist until the game runs.
detail: aurora master a2faf2cc; three coordinate spaces separated (act / plane / screen), commensurable only when v_factor is locked, verified from aeon 0bee83c6 read at a committed revision; unlocked scenes drawn hatched with the engine's own sentence; splits drawn as one-edged boundaries, palette bands not drawn and said so, because bands are intervals with two edges and drawing one as the other would misrepresent the hardware. No number from aeon's still-moving design is compiled in, and a test asserts that. Suite 5341 passing, harness 25/25 re-run by the overseer, red-first twice on the running app including a reproduction of the drawn-then-painted-black defect.

headline: The editor now warns you when a split cannot legally exist on a scrolling background — and explains why, in the engine's own terms.
matters: You could build a scene the game flatly rejects and nothing said so. The code that was supposed to warn you had a comment claiming another warning already covered it; that other warning never existed, and the claim was false for its entire 30-hour life.
detail: aurora master f704decf; sentence names the mechanism (two writers to one word — the parallax step writes the scroll at frame top, the split writes an absolute constant to the same word mid-frame) and carries both engine-named remedies rather than one. Clauses declared once, composed in three places. New currency test pins seven load-bearing claims against the engine's own refusal, identified by condition rather than line number, and skips loudly when aeon is unreachable. Suite 5356 passing; harness 36/36 re-run by the overseer; the panel rows proven discriminating by running against a build carrying master's panel (29/36, exactly the seven panel rows red).

headline: Hold Ctrl while dragging a selection and it snaps the other way — and middle-click panning works in paste mode again.
matters: Your idea, built as an invert rather than literally, because block was already the default so forcing block would have done nothing. The panning bug was the mousedown handler promising something the mousemove handler threw away — the third time today one handler enforced a rule its sibling ignored.
detail: aurora master 84d64c42; one writer feeds preview and commit so they cannot disagree, sampled live including bare Ctrl press and release against the last cursor tile; Snap control shows the effective mode and what release returns to. Pan fix pans first then falls through so the ghost tracks the post-pan cell rather than freezing. No modifier conflict, checked two ways. Suite 5362 passing; harnesses 33/33 and 17/17 re-run by the overseer on the merged tree.

headline: Painting collision no longer wipes parts of a cell it does not own — and the bits everyone believed were spare turned out to already mean something.
matters: The loop feature was about to be designed on the assumption that the top two bits of a collision cell were free. They are the second path's solidity. Nobody saw it because the build code never writes the number 14 as a literal — it refers to it by name, so a search for the value finds nothing.
detail: aurora master d5ae5a24; verified independently by the overseer at aeon b76576ea (PATH_B_SOL_SHIFT = 14, used in bake_cell, self-tested there). Aurora's own data is unaffected because it feeds the per-plane encoding which reads only path A — a narrower claim than 'the bits are free', and the currency test now pins both halves so nobody re-derives the wrong one from empty content. Writer sweep found 15 sites where reading found 3; three were broken, including the art facet's chunk brush that an enumeration by tool would miss. Suite 5383 passing; harness 12/12 re-run on the merged tree.

headline: Press X or Y to mirror a selection, or to mirror what you are about to paste.
matters: Mirrored tiles cost nothing against the tile budget — the hardware carries a flip bit per tile — so mirroring terrain was free in the data and unreachable from the editor until now.
detail: aurora master 41d303fe; one transform used at both moments, so the in-place path is literally copy-flip-write and cannot drift from the clipboard path. Mirroring is two operations — reverse the order along the axis AND toggle each word's own flip bit — and both half-transforms were planted and measured red (9/27 and 7/27 node, 32/40 CDP each). Collision flips with its own bit positions, which sit at different offsets from the art's; the crossing trap is pinned by a test. Carries the correction that bits 15:14 are path-B solidity, not spare. Suite 5421 passing; harness 40/40 re-run by the overseer on the merged tree.

headline: The collision direction marks now lead with which way is OUT, and flipping has buttons instead of only hidden keys.
matters: The marks were geometrically correct the whole time — a flat surface really did draw a flat bar with a tiny up-tick. They spent their ink on the surface direction, which is not the thing you were asking them. At 0 degrees the coloured ink went from an 11-wide-by-5-tall bar to a 1-wide-by-7-tall stem pointing up.
detail: aurora master 7da27efd; the tangent is kept, not deleted, because the silhouette is quantised to 16 integer heights and cannot distinguish 26 from 30 degrees — the bar is the only carrier of precision. Detail threshold derived from that blind band (3.576 degrees) rather than chosen: 57 screen px per cell. An undecidable wall draws a double-ended stem rather than a confident arrow. A pre-existing clip in the big preview was found and fixed. Flip buttons call the same single action the keys call; with them deleted the button harness drops to 10/25 while the key harness stays 40/40, which is what proves they are testing the buttons. Suite 5442 passing; harnesses 16/16 and 25/25 re-run by the overseer.

headline: An agent painting a big patch of tiles no longer knocks scenery out from in front of Sonic — and the same bug was hiding in the Art facet's stamp.
matters: You fixed this for the mouse last night. The same mistake had two more roads: the tool an agent uses to paint a region, and stamping a tile in the Art facet over art captured from a real section. Both silently cleared the bit that says 'this square draws in front of the player'. The Art one was invisible to a search, because it builds a cell rather than a word.
detail: O12. master 93f7870..90465c6 (pushed, remote verified). Fix routes both roads through the existing single decider core/editing/brush-word.ts: new brushPriorityFromOptional maps the wire's absent/true/false to keep/on/off, and resolveBrushPriority was split out so the cell road (composer-buffer stampTile) shares the definition of 'keep' rather than respelling it. agent-handler.ts no longer imports packNametableWord. save_chunk is a CREATOR and passes undefined as the destination, byte-identical to before. Shared entrySchema resolved by making one description true for both consumers; hf/vf now state they are NOT tri-state. Sweep: 21 writers, 2 broken (the dispatch's enumeration of 2 candidate sites was refuted — ComposerCanvas.applyTileCell was a third decider, hard-coded pri:false against docs seeded with pri: e.priority at composer-buffer.ts:57,:86). Verified by the overseer on the merged tree, not taken on report: tsc clean; suite 5,468 passed / 0 failed / 7 skipped (405 files) run twice; harness npm run harness:tile-attributes 37->49 rows, 49/49 on three independent runs (dpr=1, rect 284,74,876x721 all three, host up 3d 17h). Half the queue row was wrong and is corrected in the packet: clearing FLIPS on the agent road is correct under the shipped rule, and [w5] now pins it.

headline: An agent can now READ collision back out of the editor, so it can check a loop's shape from the data instead of squinting at a screenshot.
matters: The paint tool could write collision and nothing could read it. Two things the proposal assumed turned out false: the read could not be written back (the write filled a whole rectangle with one value, and a loop is never uniform), and a 16px cell is really four 8px cells underneath that can disagree — so the read now says 'mixed' and shows all four rather than picking one and calling it the cell.

headline: A brand-new background effect — layers that drift on their own, like clouds — can now be read and written without the editor rejecting the file.
matters: The surprise is that nothing was ever at risk of being lost. I expected the editor to quietly drop the new setting; it actually refused the whole file, because the format is closed. So a scene carrying it was unopenable rather than damaged. You still cannot AUTHOR drift — the engine side refuses it until aeon ships their half — and there is deliberately no control for it, because we already have one complaint open about a dropdown offering values the build rejects.

headline: Our own test harnesses were running a kill command that could take down a DIFFERENT Aurora than their own — including another agent's — while leaving their own stray process alive.
matters: Twenty-eight of them did this, from one shared file. It was actually seen happening on 2026-08-16 ('killed MY Electron mid-run three times') and written down as an environment quirk rather than a bug, so it sat for two weeks. They now identify their own process by descent instead of by name-matching, put your ~/.aurora/mcp.json back exactly as they found it, and refuse to talk to any Aurora they did not start. A check enforces it so the next harness written cannot skip it.
detail: O16. master 2838284..1b2e08e (merge bb5fcc5), pushed. Third hazard beyond the two dispatched: pkill -f 'aurora/dist/main/inde[x].mjs' in 28 files, living in canvas-cdp-harness.mjs session() which 15 harnesses import. It matches any Aurora whose ARGV carries the main tree's dist path and MISSES a worktree orphan -- backwards both ways. Overseer narrowed the agent's claim that it matches the owner's editor: pkill -f matches argv, and his electron-vite dev process is 'electron .', so what is established is cross-harness killing (witnessed 2026-08-16 in scratchpad/lens-sweep-2026-08-16/seat-CDP-B.json) plus a production launch from the main tree. Fixed as one shared module scratchpad/lib/harness-guard.mjs, not 98 copies; killTree gets a grace period before SIGKILL (bare SIGKILL loses Chromium's localStorage flush). Gate npm run check:harness-guards, derived from the directory. Launcher count 92->98 after the agent found two of its OWN guards vacuous under plants. Three further gate defects found by the overseer at landing, all from worktree blindness: ELOOP crash on an untracked self-referential symlink, four unguarded untracked launchers no worktree could see, and a headline counting them as clean. Verified: 141->150 classified, tracked plant exits 1, restored exits 0, tsc clean, suite 5527.

headline: You can now paint a loop's layer crossover with the same brush that draws the collision — and painting ground that is solid on both paths is one stroke instead of two.
matters: A loop needs the player to swap which collision layer they are on. Until now that was an invisible object someone had to place by hand next to every loop. Now it is part of the drawing. The brush cannot express the illegal case at all, rather than warning you about it. Two honest limits: the engine does not yet read what you paint, so a painted loop does nothing in game; and nothing writes into your real level files until aeon lands a guard against their own repaint tool erasing it.

headline: Re-checked every claim in the background-capability survey against the engine's current code. Six had drifted, including two where the fix I proposed would not have worked.
matters: That document is what gets read when we plan background work, and it had already sent two people down wrong paths in one night. Every row now carries the exact code symbol it rests on, so the next reader re-checks in one command instead of trusting a three-day-old snapshot. It also turned out the table has 25 rows, not the 21 I had written in my own note — four rows nobody was counting.
detail: O19, master 8b716f5..d17f95b, pushed. 25/25 re-measured at pinned aeon 4f846e25 and empyrean 86925008, 0 unmeasurable; 6 moved (4, 5, 6, 15, 16, plus row 11's context), 19 checked-and-unchanged recorded WITH symbols rather than by silence. Two of my own proposals corrected rather than preserved: row 6's per-band accumulator in the shadow view (Step 4a re-copies from ROM every frame and rotates, so it would build green and accumulate nothing) replaced with aeon's Parallax_Drift_Acc; row 15's bob sized the wrong mechanism entirely (whole-plane, scene-level Step-5 term, not per-band). Per-row 'measured at' markers replace the doc-wide banner. Agent found the most stale content was §E7 -- about THIS repo, no sibling read needed -- correcting the banner's premise that a peer's source has the shortest half-life. Two live-decision flags: preset binding (an authored palette band costs ROM and shows nothing) and the BG height x depth budget (OJZ act 1 is 2,048 px past its own wrap ceiling, unchecked by any build rule). Two errors found in aeon's own docs, relayed not edited.

headline: Our type checker had never looked at 127 of the test files. It does now — and turning it on immediately found a test that was passing for the wrong reason.
matters: Every 'types are clean' this project has reported, including several of mine tonight, silently skipped one directory. The nasty part is that it skipped only 30% of the tests, so the check was right often enough to keep trusting. One test was building a collision plane at half the real width and passing only because the numbers it happened to use were small enough to fit.
detail: O18, master c498506..4f347f9, pushed. Blast radius measured before fixing: 15 errors, 10 files, 5 codes; 132 files newly entered the program (782 -> 914). The gap was exactly one directory -- ~289 colocated src/**/__tests__ files were already covered by src/**/*, which is why it survived: a repo where NO tests were checked would have failed loudly the first time anyone looked. One config, not a second tsconfig: measured that test/ needs nothing extra (all 127 import vitest explicitly, no path aliases in use anywhere, no lib divergence). Compiler options byte-identical -- the entire diff is the include array plus a comment. ZERO suppressions: no ts-expect-error, no ts-ignore, no any, no excluded subtree. Real bug found: set-collision-edit.test.ts built Section.collisionEdit as Uint8Array where the field is Uint16Array; green only because its values fit in a byte. Near-miss avoided: widening isSelfMark would have made it answer false for the reserved crossover value, destroying the property that value exists to give; fixed test-side with a narrowing that throws instead. New script npm run typecheck -- cite it, never a hand-typed npx tsc, since inheriting a narrow include is the whole defect. Overseer verified: planted a type error in a test file, typecheck names it and exits non-zero, restored clean; suite 5,637/0 unchanged. Disclosed gap: scripts/ and scratchpad/ .mjs still unchecked (needs allowJs, separate decision). Overseer settled the flagged src contract: S4ActConfig.bgLayout is required non-nullable and correct -- those configs are code literals in profiles/s1.ts, all supplying real paths, so load.ts's guard is harmless defensive code, not evidence of a wrong type.

headline: A test file can no longer sit in this repo without anything running it — the suite now refuses to start if one does.
matters: The green total counted only the files the runner happened to look at. A test written in a slightly different place or with a slightly different name was type-checked, looked finished, and never ran once — and nothing anywhere would have told you.
detail: master ef00e5e (merge of worktree-agent-aac33dc49b0c7e647, 5525afd). New scripts/check-test-collection.mjs + npm run check:test-collection, chained into npm test (~0.27s). Compares two live enumerations: `vitest list --filesOnly` (asked, not re-implemented) against a walk for vitest's OWN default test-shaped glob **/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x), deliberately wider than the configured include or the check is circular. Both directions error. Empty collection = COULD NOT MEASURE, exit 2, never green. 416 on disk / 416 collected at landing. Agent proved 3 plants red; overseer independently planted a .test.mts at repo root (shape AND location untested by the agent) -> red naming the file, and independently ran the empty-include vacuity probe -> exit 2. Re-verified on the MERGED tree: 5,637 passed / 0 failed / 7 skipped, typecheck clean. O22 was booked as 'unify the two test locations'; declined as churn with no property (the move leaves the include patterns exactly as narrow) and re-shaped to this gate; the convention question goes to the owner as ergonomics. Booked O24 from the agent's own disclosed limit: collection is not execution, and 2 skipped files / 7 skipped tests are a silent zero one layer deeper.

headline: A loop crossover painted in the editor reaches the saved file exactly, and then vanishes — the ROM never sees it, and nothing would have told you.
matters: You could paint loop crossovers across a whole act, save, build, and get a ROM identical to the one you started with. Every check we have would say the build was fine, because it was. The engine half that reads the field simply is not written yet — so the editor can author something today that has no way to reach the game.
detail: LP-3, aurora 2e24094, docs/reviews/2026-08-29-crossover-paint-loop.md, instrument scratchpad/crossover-paint-harness.mjs. Throwaway aeon worktree cut from 4d86f5db, reset clean; nothing landed. document->file HOLDS (13 rows, 2 fixtures): cells written back with their own word + crossover:'hand-off' so geometry is constant by construction; exactly 16 words/plane changed in the whole 131072B file, low 14 bits identical, A=2 B=1, 2 runs of 8. Values derived from LOOP_CROSSOVER_ENCODING.md 3.2/4 at aeon 4f846e25, not from the hub's prose relay (aeon flagged their own number unverified; it was right). file->bake FAILS: collision_pipeline.py defines XOVER_* (57-75) but bake_plane_cell (229) never reads bits 15:14 — its docstring enumerates 9:0,10,11,13:12. s4.bin 06d2ccf6/719205 both sides, assembler md5 504b0c0a identical on both sides. Units finding: collattr is per-8px-subtile so a 4-cell rect moves 16 words; caught by painted:16 vs an assertion expecting 4. Instrument error kept in the packet: plane 'both' + words writes ONE plane's geometry to both (documented behaviour); row 5b caught it, and ONLY because the fixture had moved to cells with real geometry — at all-zero cells the same broken call passed 11/11. No section-0 fixture has both planes non-zero AND differing (198 runs, all identical), so two frames were run and each row's discriminating status reported.

headline: Three of our own comments promised that the engine would catch a mistake it has no code to catch — including one an AI assistant reads as a tool description.
matters: Someone reading our code would reasonably decide a bad value was safe to let through, because something downstream would reject it. Nothing does. The claims were all true of the plan and none was true of what was built.
detail: aurora d8c23f2. crossover-audit.ts ('Aeon's bake refuses these (R2)' / 'The bake hard-errors (R1)'), collision-word.ts ('a self-mark is a hard build error in aeon's bake'), editor-methods.ts ('the illegal value 3 that aeon's bake hard-errors on'). Measured: bake_plane_cell never reads bits 15:14 (docs/reviews/2026-08-29-crossover-paint-loop.md). Each now names the rule, says specified-not-implemented, and cites the measurement. Also corrected a premise relayed TO us: our audit REPORTS (agent-handler.ts:515 puts severity in the reply), it does not refuse — and Aurora cannot author value 3 at all, since crossoverFor derives it from (brush, plane) and the brush enum has no such value. That is a stronger property than a refusal and was being described as a weaker one. Fourth instance of perishable-claim-in-a-code-comment; OVERSEER.md's standing instruction was to tell the hub at a fourth, done. Shape common to all four: the comment describes an OBLIGATION on another repo and is read as a REPORT about it. Suite 5,637/0, typecheck clean.

headline: A test that quietly opts out now has to say why, or the suite fails — and on a machine without the reference game data, 165 of them were saying nothing.
matters: A skipped test and a passing test look identical in the summary line. On this machine only 7 tests skip, so the problem looked tiny; on a machine without the reference data 168 skip, and almost all of them were silent. Anyone else running our suite was reading a green number that had a large hole in it.
detail: O24, aurora master 50bc78f (merge of worktree-agent-afaa3a0949767a118). scripts/skip-report-reporter.mjs wired into vitest.config.ts reporters, so bare `npx vitest run` gets it too; 58 skipIf/skip sites across 31+ files converted to carry a reason; unexplained skip sets exit 1. OVERSEER RATIFIED the agent's ruling that silence fails rather than warns, on evidence I re-measured myself rather than accepting: with s1disasm pointed at an absent path (34 files sed'd, restored after) the tree skips 168 and skip-report says OK, every skip named — so it cannot fire spuriously on a machine lacking fixtures. MY BRIEF WAS WRONG and the agent corrected it: I called the repaired s4_engine rows exemplary; ctx.skip(reason)'s message reaches NO shipped reporter — verified here independently, the JSON reporter emits meta:{} and the marker string appears nowhere in the output. Reachable only via the Reporter API, which is why this is a reporter and not a pass over --reporter=json. Overseer plant: a reasonless describe.skip (a shape the agent's three plants did not use) -> red, with vitest's own total showing 0 failures, so the gate was the only thing catching it. Merged tree: typecheck 0, check:test-collection 418/418, npm test 5,652 passed / 0 failed / 7 skipped.

headline: Swept about 1,200 dead X-server leftovers off the machine; the harnesses that leak them are still unfixed.
matters: Test runs had been leaking a virtual display each and never cleaning up, so the machine was carrying 20 dead servers and roughly 1,200 orphaned lock and socket files, and each new run had to climb past them to find a free number. Nothing was lost and your own desktop session was never touched. This removed the mess, not the cause: four launcher scripts still leak on every run, so it will come back.
detail: O20 first half, foreground (agents cannot do process work). All 20 Xvfb had been reparented to systemd --user, were 8.5-35 h old, and every one had zero client fds; killed by PID individually, never pkill. Residue was far larger than the booked row: 943 locks / 264 sockets against ONE live X server (Xwayland :0), hence display numbers climbing to :1030. Removed 941 locks + 263 sockets with a live-PID guard, keeping :0. The guard held back :151, whose recorded PID had been RECYCLED onto a Vivaldi renderer thread - so a PID-liveness check on a lock file is two-valued ('that PID is in use' != 'that X server runs'), the same family as [ -S socket ] reporting a corpse as a server. Removed it on the stronger instrument: wrong process class plus no socket. Cause (4 unguarded launchers) open.

headline: Six tests had been reporting PASSED while touching nothing at all, and no run could ever have told you.
matters: On any machine without the reference game data our suite was lying three different ways: 59 tests said Aurora was broken when the truth was just that the data is not there, three files died on the spot and took 29 more tests with them, and six sat in the green column having never looked at their subject. That last group is the one worth knowing about: two of them could only ever have worked inside a temporary folder an assistant creates, so on your machine they had been measuring nothing for their whole life, and there was no input in the world that could have turned them red. Run the suite with the reference data hidden now and it reports 269 honest skips and zero failures.
detail: O25, merge 0c3e73c (branch o25-fixture-absent-honesty, 5 commits). Class A 59 -> 0, Class B 3 files/29 tests -> 0, Class C 6 -> 0, plus 58 rows that never registered at all. Cause of class C: a bare `return` from a test body IS a pass, and console.warn reaches no reporter, total or exit code, so the skip-reason gate landed at 50bc78f is structurally blind to it -- failure and success emit the same artifact. Worst case aeon-json-trailing-newline.test.ts:233 resolve(__dirname,'../../../../../../aeon') = six levels: /aeon from the main checkout, the real path only from a linked worktree (verified by arithmetic, both directions). New gate scripts/check-pseudo-skip.mjs wired into npm test ahead of vitest. OVERSEER-VERIFIED FIRSTHAND, not branch-side: gate red on a clean extraction of 1e7c288 (exit 1, 9 sites); matcher poisoned -> 'scanned 0 bodies in 419 files ... COULD NOT MEASURE' exit 2, ruling out the alternative green path; merged tree tsc exit 0 and 5,656 passed/7 skipped/0 failed; true absence via tmpfs-over-sibling-root in a private namespace 5,332 passed/269 reasoned skips/0 failed exit 0. OPEN, agent-disclosed and I reproduced their exact numbers by an independent condition (empty dirs rather than absent): a PARTIAL checkout still fails 27 files/135 tests, because every guard tests directory existence.

headline: The curve dropdown no longer offers you a setting the build will reject — it is greyed out with the reason on it.
matters: Picking a curve target equal to Plane B's own speed makes a ramp that goes nowhere, and the build refuses it. Until now you could pick it and only afterwards be told. It is greyed now, labelled '(engine refuses)', with the full sentence underneath — deliberately NOT hidden, because a missing option teaches nothing and reads as a bug. Screenshots are in scratchpad/shots-curve-option-disabled/. One rough edge left alone: the closed box clips the last bracket at the current column width, and widening it would move four other rows that are measured against it.
detail: O13, merge 7609750 (branch o13-curve-option-disabled). curveGoesNowhere/curveFlatReason are the single source; curveAdvisory and the new curveFieldOptions both read them and the component holds NO fb comparison (verified here by grep on the merged tree), so picker and advisory cannot drift. Merged-tree re-verify: tsc clean, 5,661 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed, all three gates green; captures viewed firsthand, not accepted by description. TWO PLANTS CAME BACK GREEN AND WERE DIAGNOSED: the wiring test's slice ran to end-of-file and swept in two OTHER pickers sharing the identical disabled={o.disabled} line, so deleting the flag left them holding it green (cause ii, two paths one observable); slice now bounded and the bound itself asserted. Harness row 3f 'no other option is disabled' was trivially true when none was; it names which one now. OVERSEER RULING: do NOT widen to vsplitLockAdvisory. The repo's own test (tableRefParamOptions vs factor0_lock) is disable only when no document content can make the value legal; vsplit's precondition is another control's v_factor in the same document, so it stays advise-don't-disable. Idiom was already here twice; tableRefParamOptions is the banner the drift and band parcels should copy, not this file.

headline: You can now write a colour band in the editor — and the panel says plainly that saving does not put it in the game.
matters: This is the authoring half of the parallax/raster work: a band you write here becomes real ROM data through aeon's generator. Three things it still cannot do are printed at the top of the panel, above every control, not hidden in a tooltip: saving does not install the band (a programmer binds it by hand); seeing it at all is a debug key combination whose list your document does not join by itself; and nothing anywhere checks that a band is VISIBLE, so a legal band over an unused palette colour builds fine and shows nothing. It also says outright that nobody in the suite has ever looked at one of these on screen, so there is no preview — an unfaithful one would be worse than none.
detail: EW-BAND, merge a44d91c (branch ew-band-preset-panel). Codec + vendored schema + provenance, full plumbing, provider owning every rule, BandPresetPanel mounted in the effects column. Anchors both re-derived by the agent AND by me: aeon docs/EDITOR_RASTER_PRESETS.md blob 94db6b3a (read past the revert window at 23006094), empyrean schema blob 29c1c5ee at 6664b61, identical at origin/main. Page and schema agree on all seven machine-checked rows. SCOPE HELD: document shape is settled so it is built; band anchoring to layout/camera is out (design absent from aeon's queue; owner sequenced moving bands after). SHARED-MODULE CHANGE, the risky part: json-schema-subset.ts refused unevaluatedProperties beside ANY in-place applicator; the preset schema is the first to pair it with a required-only oneOf, which annotates nothing, so that was a false positive. Now a prover over a WHITELIST of provably-inert keywords ($ref still unconditional refusal). I verified it BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by reading the rationale: required-only ACCEPTS; properties, additionalProperties, an unrecognised keyword, and an annotator nested under `not` each REFUSE with UnsupportedSchemaError, and I printed which path each took rather than trusting a bare toThrow — my own first probe passed 3 rows vacuously by calling a non-existent export. Merged tree: tsc clean, 5,724 passed / 7 skipped / 0 failed, 422 files collected. Agent self-caught two defects incl. a harness that polluted its own fixture and passed on it. TAGGED: still nobody has seen a band on screen; aeon's cycle-table lint unexercised from this side.

headline: Cleared out the development leftovers: four abandoned working copies and forty-one finished branches.
matters: Every one of them was work already merged into the main line, so nothing was lost, and I checked that before deleting rather than after. Two files pointing at a dead Aurora process are gone too. If you go looking for an old branch by name it will not be there any more, so I saved a list of every name with its exact position, which restores any of them in one command.

headline: A stamped chunk now remembers where it came from — the groundwork for fixing a chunk once and having every copy follow.
matters: This is the shape you asked for: remembering is the default, and detaching is the deliberate act, so a wrong guess is always recoverable. It survives closing and reopening the project. Nothing has changed on screen yet — there is no checkbox and no live updating — because anything visible has to be proven by driving the real app, and that is the next piece. The one thing worth knowing: the classic half of the editor could not be copied, for a reason in the data rather than the code, so this is a second mechanism and not a shared one.
detail: Owner ruling d-18c, phase 1. Merge 39e4905 (merge commit e831caf, branch feat/aeon-chunk-identity, 3 agent commits). Section.chunkLinks = per-TILE Uint32Array plane of stable placement ids beside the nametable + ChunkPlacementLink records; persisted as a new section_N.chunklinks.json sidecar. Classic's approach (level IS a grid of chunk ids) is unavailable because aeon's tileGrid.nametable IS the exported artifact and a ChunkDef is a variable widthTiles x heightTiles footprint, so one id per cell cannot say which PART of a chunk a cell holds. OVERSEER VERIFICATION on the merged tree: tsc clean; 5783 passed / 7 skipped vs base c4534d3 at 5724/7 measured in the SAME tree (+59, skips unchanged). A first base run in a separate worktree read 5717/14 and was discarded as an environment difference, not code -- both sides re-measured in one tree rather than stitched across two. Two violations planted independently of the agent's 13: (a) dropping the chunkLinks carry from cloneSection -> exactly one row red, 'cloneSection must carry chunkLinks: expected undefined to be defined', while the pre-existing key-set guard stayed GREEN, confirming the agent's own disclosure that it derives from createSection and cannot see an optional field (bar 12); (b) defeating the understood() gate in buildAeonSavePlan -> the row asserting a refused sidecar is NOT overwritten went red. Both restored. Two existing map-stamp rows changed expectation on purpose and both are STRENGTHENINGS: (f) keeps the surviving half of the old property and adds the detached-form-is-null discriminator; (g) trades toHaveLength(1) for an explicit no-collision-child assertion. Persistence handles the section-meta erasure defect class explicitly: a refused sidecar is left on disk, and the test asserts the refusal stayed SCOPED (other section files still saved). OVERSEER ADDITION at landing (39e4905): row 91 now names the ORDERING CONSTRAINT -- wire the renderer brush link-breaks (seam 4) before or with the propagation call (seam 3), never after. buildActPropagationCommand verified to have no caller in src/ (tests only), so the gap is latent today; wiring propagation first would silently overwrite hand-painted art with library tiles.

headline: Fix a chunk once and every copy of it in the level fixes itself — with a checkbox for the copies you want left alone.
matters: This finishes what you asked for. Stamping remembers by default, so correcting a chunk corrects the whole level; ticking the box makes a stamp a plain copy that nothing will touch again, and you can detach one you already placed. Hand-painting over part of a stamp detaches only the tiles you painted, so your touch-ups are never overwritten. Proven by driving the real editor and clicking the real controls, not by unit tests — the tests cannot see the screen. One limit worth knowing: copies stamped in OTHER acts keep their link but are not updated yet.
detail: Owner ruling d-18c phase 2. Merge 84e3092f (branch feat/chunk-identity-ui; 6656e747 brush link-breaks, 4f88ac9f checkbox+detach, 5e7f9b5f propagation). ORDERING CONSTRAINT (overseer's finding at phase-1 landing) honoured and verified, not trusted: link-breaking landed two commits BEFORE propagation. VERIFICATION on the merged tree: tsc clean; 5799 passed / 7 skipped vs master 5789/7 measured in the same tree (+10, skips unchanged). CDP harness re-run by the overseer in the foreground FOUR times across two rebuilds, 10/10 each, dpr + canvas rect printed per run (dpr=1 observed; the agent additionally ran it at 1.35, so both regimes this box produces are covered). OVERSEER'S OWN PLANT, independent of the agent's seven: cutting link-breaking at the endPaintStroke site ONLY -> row 6 RED, row 7 GREEN, proving the three near-identical set-tiles dispatches are genuinely distinguished (the documented hazard where a plant in the wrong one survives a full cycle looking convincing). Row 10 also reddened, catching the exact damage the ordering constraint exists to prevent. Restored, 10/10. Agent's own disclosures verified as honest: row 1 is the anti-vacuous gate only, and row 10 stays green under poison F (with nothing propagating, 'it did not touch the hand-painted tiles' is vacuously true) - recorded in the poison file rather than counted. Agent also corrected a wrong prediction of its own in place (poison C reddens rows 2/3, not 2/8). OPEN, documented not glossed: cross-act propagation (buildActPropagationCommand is indexed by flat act slot and one command belongs to one act's undo stack); the harness never saves, so the sidecar round trip of gesture-written links rests on phase 1's node tests.

headline: An agent can now read and write the raster presets an author builds by hand — the first of the two effects pieces you approved is on master.
matters: The band presets that drive the raster effects could only be edited by a person clicking in the panel. Now a Claude agent can list them, read one whole, and write one back, going through the exact same rules the panel does — so an agent and a person cannot disagree about what is refused. Two things are worth knowing. The queue row promised this was pure wiring over a finished provider; the agent building it found that was true of every EDIT and false of whole-document REPLACE, and said so instead of quietly filling the gap — the row now records its own error. And the deliberately missing fourth tool, the one that would bind a preset to a place in the level, is still missing on purpose: there is no field on a section to write it into until aeon lands one.
